plan.notes: Source: Dutchess Community College 2024-25 Catalog, Computer Science (CPS) Program Map, pp. 136-138 (official DCC site PDF: https://www.sunydutchess.edu/_resources/pdfs/dcc-catalog-2024-25-archive-web.pdf). The Associate in Science (A.S.) in Computer Science (CPS) is DCC's true degree name for this program (transfer-oriented CS program). Transcription: term-by-term sequence manually transcribed from the catalog program map; course titles, credit hours, and prerequisite/corequisite statements verified against the same catalog's course-descriptions section. Program note: students should be at Math Placement Level 4 or higher. CPS 141 has an official corequisite of MAT 184 or higher (co-enrolled with the first-semester math choice slot); it carries no printed prerequisite. Official prerequisite grade rules (e.g., CPS 142 requires CPS 141 with a C or better; ENG 102 requires ENG 101 with a C or better) are course-code sequencing here per schema; the 'C or better' grade detail is not encoded. Catalog footnotes carried: (a) Students must complete MAT 222 to satisfy the CPS degree requirements. (b) Elective courses: MAT 186 or MAT 223 or MAT 230 or second semester of science sequence recommended; many four-year colleges require a two-semester sequence in physics or chemistry. (c) Physics or Chemistry or Biology recommended; applicable four-credit courses are in astronomy, biology, chemistry, geology, physical sciences, physics; students select from General Education Category B Natural Sciences. (d) Free elective: subject area for Computer Science includes all courses labeled CPS. (e) General Education Elective: courses from General Education categories Social Sciences, The Arts, World History and Global Awareness, and World Languages. Credit-range honesty: catalog prints Elective (b) slots as 3-4 credits and semester totals as ranges (16-17, 14-15, 15-16); the catalog's published 'Total Required Minimum Semester Hours Credit 62' corresponds to 3-credit electives, so plan uses 3 for each Elective (b) slot (17+16+14+15=62). 4-credit electives would raise the degree total above 62. No 0-credit required courses or milestones in this plan. 'US History and Civic Engagement' (2024-25 catalog wording) is a General Education category choice, replacing the older 'American History (Appendix D)' row.
